Stated Claim / Post Context:
Store says AI-generated receipt was used to secure fraudulent purse refund

Employees said a fake receipt was used to get a warranty refund on a purse the store doesn't carry.

Actual Article Body:
ALICE, Texas (KIII) — Employees at Horseshoes Western Wear said they are learning a new lesson about protecting the business after a fake, apparently AI-generated receipt was used to obtain a warranty refund.

Manager Inez Almaraz said the store’s owner learned from a distributor that a receipt appearing to be AI-generated was used to get a warranty refund for a purse.

“We’ve never had anything or any of this happen, especially with something that we carry. For them to produce or generate a fake AI receipt is something that’s just not tolerated,” Almaraz said.

Almaraz said the purse involved was a Consuela designer purse, which the store carries and sells.

“Consuela is a designer purse, and we are fortunate to be able to carry it and sell it,” Almaraz said.

The distributor fell victim to the fake receipt before it was identified as fraudulent.

A comparison of the real receipt and the fake showed differences, including the wrong address.

Retail seller Angel Ramos said employees found the discrepancy because the store did not carry the purse listed on the fake receipt.

“Just be more cautious. Look at your receipts. Pay attention to your systems. Just keep track of your inventory because we didn’t carry that purse,” Ramos said.

The Better Business Bureau says artificial intelligence is making it easier for scammers to create convincing documents, meaning businesses can’t always rely on obvious mistakes to spot a fake.

Katie Galan with the Better Business Bureau said scammers rely on urgency to avoid detection.

“What they want is for you to rush and to not have the time to verify, to ask questions, to look at that receipt a little closer. So, that’s what they prey on, is us being in so much of a rush that we don’t have time to double-check things,” Galan said.

Almaraz said she hopes sharing the store’s experience will help other small businesses avoid the same situation.

“We never thought it would happen to us, and we didn’t even know something like that even existed. If it happened to us, it can happen to anybody,” Almaraz said.
